# P4.5 Probe evidence integrity: the write precondition and complete redaction

## Objective
Two properties of the one script that writes `docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`,
both owner-authorised on 2026-09-29 (`state/AMENDMENTS.md` AM-070) and both
carried out of P4.1 by its own reviews rather than fixed inside it.

1. **The probe checks that it was *run* before it writes anything.** Today the
   entry-point guard at `scripts/v2/probe-redirects.mjs:531` is the only thing
   between an import and seven `HEAD`s plus an overwrite of the record of record,
   and the suite can only notice a regression in it *after* `main()` has already
   written the file — DEF-2, `docs/v2/state/reviews/P4.1-attempt3-impl.md:340-361`.
   `main()` must re-assert the guard as its first statement, before the first
   request, and the regression must be observable without a human diffing the
   evidence file.
2. **Nothing that could be a credential, and nothing that could break the record
   as markdown, reaches the evidence file.** `redactQuery`
   (`probe-redirects.mjs:296-299`) truncates only from the first `?`, so a
   `Location` carrying user-info, or a fragment, or a fragment that looks like a
   query, is written verbatim; and a decoded query **name** carrying a character
   markdown acts on is written raw into the record.

The path is the one input class this card deliberately does **not** redact, and
Fixed decision 6 says why, with a test that pins the decision so a later change
has to be conscious.

## Fixed decisions
1. **The write precondition, and the one place it may sit.** One new exported
   function, `assertMayWriteEvidence()`: if `isEntryPoint()` (`:516-529`) is
   false it throws an `Error` whose message says the probe was imported rather
   than run and names `docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md` as the file it refused
   to write; otherwise it returns `undefined`. It is called as the **first
   statement of `main()`** — before the loop at `:473`, therefore before every
   `fetch` and before `mkdir`/`writeFile` at `:486-487`. Not after the loop, not
   in the write helper, and not only in the tests.
   *Why in the script and not only in the suite:* with the last line regressed to
   a bare `await main();`, an import now runs `main()`, `main()` refuses on its
   first statement, and the evidence file is untouched — so the regression
   becomes harmless first and detected second, in that order. The throw is
   deliberate: a silent `return` would make the regression invisible, which is
   exactly the failure mode DEF-2 names.
2. **The evidence file is the oracle, and the check is installed before the
   import.** The suite reads `docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md` into a buffer at
   module top, **before** the dynamic import at `:101`, and asserts byte equality
   twice: in a named case, and in the `after()` hook that already exists at
   `:102-104`. Read-only — neither file writes it, and the path comes from the
   repository root the same way `evidencePath` does (`:85-86`). This converts
   "discovered only by diffing against a previous run"
   (`P4.1-attempt3-impl.md:350-353`) into a failure the suite reports itself.
   Both places are required: a case can be reordered or skipped, a hook cannot.
3. **`redactQuery` truncates at whichever of `?` or `#` occurs first in the
   string, and keeps that delimiter** — so a query-then-fragment
   `Location` (`…?a=1#f=2`) renders `<prefix>?<redacted>`, a fragment-then-query
   one (`…#f=2?a=1`) renders `<prefix>#<redacted>`, and a lone query or a lone
   fragment renders exactly as today. A string with neither delimiter is
   returned unchanged, also exactly as today. The rule is about **position, not
   about which delimiter is more dangerous**: the first of the two is where the
   unverifiable tail of the value begins, so everything from it onward goes,
   whichever one it is.
   *Why the order cannot be "the first `#` whenever there is one":* that reads
   like a stricter rule and is the opposite, because on a query-then-fragment
   `Location` it truncates at the `#` and pastes the whole query, values
   included, directly beneath the `query:` field at `:338`, whose own text reads
   `present — <redacted>, never pasted` — a line that reads as redacted and is
   not, the failure `cards/P4.1.md:504-512` named. The header's own claim at
   `:26-28` is only true for the position rule, and Objective 2's "nothing that
   could be a credential" is only true for the position rule. The fragment-first
   shape is still the one today's code gets wrong: `…#token=1?x=2` currently
   redacts to `…#token=1?<redacted>`, which reads as redacted and is not
   (`P4.1.md:506-509`) — under the position rule it becomes `…#<redacted>`; the
   query-then-fragment shape is the one an over-broad rule breaks, and case 10
   pins it. Nothing is lost by truncating early: the record already carries
   `query:` (`:338`), `fragment:` (`:351`) and the `fragment_present` refusal
   (`:264`) as separate fields, so the raw line is the convenience copy, not
   the only copy.
4. **User-info is never written.** When the authority carries an `@`, everything
   before the last `@` that precedes the first `/`, `?` or `#` is replaced with
   `<redacted>` and the `@` is kept, so `https://user:pass@host/p` renders as
   `https://<redacted>@host/p` and the host still reads. This is a credential by
   definition and removing it costs nothing: `userInfo` already records whether
   one was present (`:288`, `:350`) and rule 1 already refuses it (`:263`).
5. **A name is escaped for markdown at the point of display, and nowhere else.**
   One new exported pure function, `escapeMarkdownInline(value)`: it replaces every
   C0 control character (U+0000-U+001F), U+007F, U+0060 (backtick), U+005C
   (backslash) and U+007C (vertical bar) with the visible escape `\uXXXX` in
   lowercase hex, and touches nothing else — a name is escaped, never dropped,
   never truncated, so a plan editor still reads every character of a name an
   allow-list might have to gain. It is applied at exactly four display sites:
   the name interpolated into the `query_key_not_allowed` sentence (`:271`), the
   name list in `renderArtifact` (`:347`), and the two `redactQuery` outputs
   (`:333`, `:367`).
   *The two properties that keep this a rendering change and not a guard change
   (HS-7), and both are asserted:* the membership test at `:270` runs on the
   **decoded, unescaped** name, and `describeLocation` returns `queryKeys`
   **unescaped** (`:287`). The backticks the code writes itself
   (`` `query_key_not_allowed` ``) live in the template, not in the value, so
   they survive; only a backtick that arrived inside a name is escaped.
6. **The path is written as observed. This is a decision with a reason, not an
   oversight, and it is the one thing a reviewer should attack hardest.** A token
   embedded in a path is generically indistinguishable from a CDN's own
   content-addressed path: the one record that exists carries two 64-hex path
   components that are the artifact's content and not secrets
   (`P4.1-attempt4-impl.md:250`), and the same review confirmed the committed
   file has no `#`, no authority `@`, and no `?` other than `?<redacted>`, with
   `user-info: absent` and `fragment: absent` on every artifact. Redacting
   "token-shaped" path segments would mean **inventing a new threshold inside this
   card**, which is precisely what HS-7 forbids and what no owner has authorised.
   So: no path redaction; a named test pins the deliberate preservation, so a
   blanket redaction later is a conscious change with its own evidence; and the
   residual is recorded in the return file and in `docs/v2/evidence/P4.5/`. What
   is still guaranteed about a path is unchanged — it is written only after rule 1
   has judged scheme, port, user-info, fragment and every query name
   (`:261-274`), and a `Location` that fails any of those is a recorded refusal,
   not a silent write.
7. **Nothing else about the record changes.** Same verdicts, same
   `UNDETERMINED` sentinel, same refusal sentences, same sort order and
   de-duplication in `queryKeyNames`, same host table (`:429-435`), same prose in
   `render`, same `exit` behaviour in `main`. No new export beyond the two named
   in decisions 1 and 5; no removed export.
8. **No egress, no new run, no new grant.** This card runs the probe **zero**
   times. P4.1's V2 stays `NOT RUN`, its grant stays spent, and AM-070 authorises
   no network of any kind — not a `HEAD`, not a re-resolution, not a DNS lookup.
   Every case is proven offline against the renderer with an injected `fetch` that
   throws (`:97-100`, already in place). That is why the fixtures are loopback
   literals and derived catalogue URLs and never a vendor: a vendor literal in a
   `.test.mjs` file fails V2 and fixing that would mean editing `eslint.config.js`,
   which is not editable.

## Steps
1. **Tests first.** Add the eleven cases below, run V1, and record that they fail on
   the unmodified probe — each for the reason its row names, not for a shared
   reason like an import error.
2. **The write precondition** (Fixed decision 1): add `assertMayWriteEvidence`
   and call it as `main()`'s first statement.
3. **The evidence-bytes check** (Fixed decision 2): read the file into a buffer
   before the import, assert in the named case and in `after()`.
4. **The redaction changes** (Fixed decisions 3, 4, 5): `redactQuery`, then
   `escapeMarkdownInline`, then the four call sites. Re-run V1 after each of the
   three, so a regression is attributable to one change.
5. Run V1, V2, then **V3 last** (Fixed decision 8 and the row's own note: V3 is
   the only row that touches the evidence file, so nothing else may read it
   first). Write each row's command, exit code, times and output excerpt into
   `docs/v2/evidence/P4.5/` with sandbox paths written `<sandbox>` and the home
   folder `~` (RUN-CONFIG §4), and record in the return file: the eleven case
   names, the residual from Fixed decision 6, and the fact that this card does
   not answer the open §4 hostname ruling. Leave the change uncommitted for the
   coordinator.

| # | Case | What it asserts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | write precondition refuses in an import context | `assertMayWriteEvidence()` throws when called from the suite (where `isEntryPoint()` is false, `:138`), and the message names the evidence file it refused to write |
| 2 | the evidence file is byte-identical before and after this suite | the buffer read before the import equals the file's bytes when the case runs, and again in `after()`; a run that mutated the file fails here rather than in a human diff |
| 3 | a query is redacted and a query-less `Location` is left alone | unchanged from today's case at `:311-315`: `…?a=secret` becomes `…?<redacted>`, a query-less URL comes back unchanged |
| 4 | a fragment is redacted and never pasted | a fabricated `#fabricated-fragment-token=1` appears nowhere in the record, the line ends `#<redacted>`, and `fragment: present — refused` is still recorded beside it |
| 5 | a fragment that looks like a query is redacted whole | `…/p#fabricated-fragment-token=1?fabricated-fragment-value`: neither the fragment nor the fake value survives — the exact shape P4.1 named and today's `redactQuery` gets wrong |
| 6 | user-info is redacted and the host still reads | the record shows `<redacted>@` and neither the fabricated user nor the fabricated password appears anywhere in it, while `user-info: present — refused` and the hostname both still read |
| 7 | a path segment is written as observed, deliberately | a fabricated path component survives verbatim in the record — the pin for Fixed decision 6, so a later blanket redaction cannot arrive unnoticed |
| 8 | a name decoding to a markdown-active character is escaped, never dropped | a name decoding to U+0060 and one decoding to CR LF render as the literal `\u0060` and `\u000d\u000a` escapes, the name is still present in escaped form, and the record contains no raw newline inside a name and no code span the record's own quoting does not close |
| 9 | the refusal message and the redacted line escape what they quote | the escaped form appears in the `query_key_not_allowed` sentence and in the `exact Location` line, while `describeLocation(...).queryKeys` is **un**escaped and byte-identical to today — the assertion that keeps Fixed decision 5 on the display side of the membership test |
| 10 | a query then a fragment redacts at the `?`, and the query value never lands | a fabricated `…/p?X-Fabricated=<value>#fabricated-fragment=<v>` renders as `…/p?<redacted>` — the first delimiter in the string, kept — and neither fabricated value appears anywhere in the record, while `query: present — <redacted>, never pasted` and the `fragment_present` refusal are both still recorded. This is the order case 5's mirror image and the gate on Fixed decision 3: an implementation that truncates at the first `#` *whenever one exists* fails here, having pasted the query below a line that says it was never pasted |
| 11 | the unparseable branch's raw line escapes what it quotes | a **relative** `Location` that `new URL()` rejects, carrying a U+0060 and a CR LF, renders at `:333` as `raw, query redacted:` with the literal `\u0060` and `\u000d\u000a` escapes and no raw newline inside the value; `record incomplete:` (`:330`) and every `not determined` field are still there. That branch writes a header value straight through with no URL parse in between, so it is the fourth display site decision 5 names and the one most likely to carry arbitrary bytes — it has no gate anywhere else |

## Stop conditions
1. **The precondition cannot be `main()`'s first statement** — some real caller
   reaches `main()` without being the entry point. Record the caller and the
   error and report `BLOCKED`. Do not move the check later, do not weaken it to a
   warning, and do not satisfy it by editing `scripts/package-mac.sh` or
   `installer/` (HS-9). A precondition after the loop is not this fix and is
   worse than nothing, because it would read as one.
2. **Escaping a name changes a decision.** If any implementation makes
   `describeLocation().queryKeys` escaped, or makes the membership test at `:270`
   compare an escaped name, or makes an admitted name stop being admitted — stop.
   Escaping belongs on the display side only (Fixed decision 5), and the fix is to
   move it, never to relax case 9 or to widen an `allowedQueryKeys` value.
3. **A `Location` whose *path* carries something that looks like a credential is
   observed in a real run.** This card does not run the probe, so this can only
   arrive as a report: record the exact `Location` with its query and fragment
   written `<redacted>`, report `BLOCKED`, and name the plan-editor action. Whether
   the path rule changes is the coordinator's and the owner's — a new redaction
   threshold is a contract-shaped decision (HS-7) and never one made inside this
   card.
4. **A fixture needs a non-loopback URL literal.** Derive from the catalogue or
   use `127.0.0.1`; a real vendor host fails V2 and is not a reason to edit
   `eslint.config.js` or to assemble a URL out of fragments to slip past the
   selector, which is loosening a guard (HS-7, Fixed decision 8).
5. **`docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md` is already different from its committed
   content when this card starts.** Stop before running anything, do not run V3,
   and report: the record of record is not this card's to reconcile, and
   regenerating or hand-editing it is outside every clause above.
6. **Either item turns out to need a change outside May edit** — `installer/`,
   `eslint.config.js`, a contract, a threshold, a host rule, a query allowance, an
   `ALLOWED` entry, the `writeFile` order in `main()`, or another card's file.
   Report it as a finding for the coordinator and change nothing (HS-7, HS-9).
   AM-070 authorises exactly this card's two items and nothing else.
7. **V1 or V2 fails in a file outside May edit**, or the new suite cannot be made
   to fail on the unfixed probe: stop and report. A green suite that cannot fail
   is worse than no suite, and that is the defect DEF-2 is actually about.

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-ACQ@1 Acquisition and readiness

**Built by** P4.1. **Proven by** P4.1, P4.4, S4b.1. **Consumers:** installer,
setup screens, Spanish speech acquisition.

**Requests**
1. `https:` only; port absent or 443; no user-info; no fragment; no query
   unless the artifact's manifest entry lists allowed query keys.
2. Host must be in the artifact's `allowedHosts` (initial) or
   `allowedRedirectHosts` (redirects) in `ACQUISITION.md`.
3. `redirect: 'manual'`. Each `Location` is resolved and validated **before**
   it is requested. At most 5 hops; a repeated URL is a loop and fails.
   No custom headers are sent to any host.
4. Checksum verification stays separate and mandatory.

**Readiness**
5. A model file is ready only if it is a regular file (not a directory or
   symlink to one), its size equals the pinned size, and either a receipt
   `<file>.receipt.json` records the pinned SHA-256 with matching size,
   mtime and inode, or a fresh hash matches. A fresh matching hash also
   establishes readiness without writing a receipt. Readiness probes never
   write receipts; explicit acquisition or repair writes a receipt only after
   verification.
6. Wrong size, wrong hash, directory, stale pin or dangling `.part` →
   state `invalid` with a code; repair only after the user presses Start.
7. Ollama pulls are performed by the daemon, outside these checks. The
   installer verifies the resulting tag's digest with `ollama show` and
   reports it; it cannot enforce the daemon's network behaviour, and the
   docs say so.

**Protocol.** The existing JSON-lines protocol (`installer/src/protocol.ts`)
stays the only one. Additions are optional fields. Exactly one terminal
event per run (`done` or `failed`). Cancel sends SIGTERM to the installer's
own process group only.

**Rejection examples.** Initial URL `https://huggingface.co:8443/…` → refused
before contact. Redirect to a host not listed → refused before contact.
11-byte file at the model path → `invalid`, not ready.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.

**Redirect admission (rule 1).** A redirect is followed only when its `Location`
resolves to `https:`, port 443, no user-info, no fragment, a host the row's
*Redirect hosts* cell admits, and a query whose every parameter name appears in
that row's *Allowed query keys* cell. A parameter name outside the cell is
refused (`query_key_not_allowed`) before the URL is requested. `none` means the
row admits no query at all, so any query is `query_not_allowed` — that is the
default and it is unchanged. No row admits a query by wildcard, a prefix or a
blanket permission, and the cell is the complete list: adding a name is a
plan-editor amendment (AM-042).

**Why A07's names are safe to enumerate.** The ten names are the AWS
CloudFront signed-URL parameter set plus Hugging Face's Xet and
`response-content-*` parameters, observed on 2026-09-26 across all six C-STT
artifacts and the one speech artifact, each answering `302` to
`us.aws.cdn.hf.co` (`docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`). They cannot change
*which* bytes arrive: the path is fixed by the pinned catalogue URL and the
bytes are verified against the pinned `sha256`, and the committed name is the
entry's own `sizeBytes` path, so the two `response-content-*` parameters can
only shape headers a client would have sent anyway. The card's own worry — "a
query string is where a download URL turns into a message" — is about
*outbound* data, and none of these names carries any: the probe records the
**names** only and writes every value as `<redacted>`, so a signature is never
in the repository, the evidence or any log.

**The four-arm comparison (A13, A14, A15).** Added 2026-09-26 on the owner's
approval, for one measurement round and nothing else. The arms are
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` as the control (A08; already present, and A08's "never pulled
if present" still holds), plus A13, A14 and A15. Three rules bind the round and
are not negotiable per run:

1. **No candidate becomes a default.** A07's "selected one only" and A08's tag
   are unchanged. The round measures; it does not promote.
2. **The licence of A14 and A15 is unknown to the coordinator and must be found
   before either is pulled.** These are models downloaded by the user at setup,
   so L-POLICY@1's row for that applies: per the publisher's licence, shown and
   recorded. Prism's licence for these repositories is not asserted here because
   it was not verified — anyone pulling them records the licence text and the
   URL it came from, or reports `BLOCKED`. Guessing it is exactly the failure
   this manifest exists to prevent.
3. **The GPU is not shared.** One model loaded at a time, `keep_alive` set so
   each unloads after its arm, and no arm runs while the owner is testing on the
   machine or a live instance is in use. A four-arm run is long and real.

**Fraunces (A16) follows Kalam, not a build-time download.** Both source TTFs live in `docs/v2/assets/` with their OFL texts, and `build-brand-fraunces.py` reads the local file and touches no network — regenerating the wordmark in six years must not depend on a `/tmp` file or a download working. A16 permits exactly that one fetch, to obtain the file committed beside it. Fraunces is a **variable** font; the committed cut is the variable one, and the generator pins `wght 500`, `opsz 14`, `SOFT 0`, `WONK 0`, because a static instance could not set optical size and an unpinned variable font would not reproduce. The TTF is never bundled: the app ships outlines only.

**Owner-run items.** `apt` needs `sudo`. The coordinator writes the exact
command to `docs/v2/state/OWNER-ACTIONS.md`, stops the dependent cards, and
waits; the owner runs it. Agents never enter a password.

**Ollama.** Before any pull, run `ollama list`; if the tag exists, do not pull.
Record the digest with `ollama show <tag>`. Real-model runs set Ollama's
`keep_alive` so evaluation models unload after use, and run only one model
at a time, to avoid starving the live instance.

## 2. Development tools already present

Anything already installed on the PC (git, Python, Piper if present,
whisper-cli, Ollama) may be used as found. Record its version in evidence.

## 3. L-POLICY@1 Licences

One rule, applied per object reviewed (a tool, a library, a model file, a
voice, a dictionary, generated audio are separate objects).

| Object | Allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Code or data **shipped** in the app or installer | MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, Zlib, 0BSD, Unicode, OFL-1.1 (fonts), CC0, CC-BY-4.0 (data, with attribution) |
| The one pre-approved exception | Spanish dictionary **data** under an MPL option of a multi-licence, shipped unmodified in its own files, election and obligations stated in `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and `docs/decisions.md` |
| Development-only tools never shipped or linked | any OSI licence, including GPL (Piper) |
| Generated fixtures committed to the repo | only if the voice's model card permits redistribution of generated audio; otherwise generate at test time into the sandbox and never commit |
| Models downloaded by the user at setup | per the publisher's licence, shown in setup, recorded in the catalogue |
| System libraries bundled into an AppImage (for example WebKitGTK, LGPL) | allowed for **test builds**; **public distribution requires owner review** (listed in the final report) |

Anything else: do not add it; the card reports `BLOCKED` with the licence
text found. A dependency's MIT wrapper does not change its data's licence.
